title: Normative boundaries of AI in scientific work: Evidence from PhD researchers
abstract: arXiv:2608.25678v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in scientific work, but researchers may not evaluate its use uniformly across research tasks. This study examines task-specific attitudes towards AI among an international, self-selected sample of 3,785 PhD students in STEM and medical and health sciences who participated in Nature's Graduate Survey 2025. We analyse respondents' comfort with using AI for writing a research article, collecting and analysing data, designing experiments, tracking scientific literature, and summarising it. Latent class analysis identifies four distinct attitudinal profiles. The dominant profile reflects a "division of labour," in which AI is widely accepted for literature-related tasks but resisted in activities closely associated with intellectual contribution, such as writing, data analysis, and experimental design. translated_title: 科学工作中人工智能的规范性边界：来自博士研究人员的证据
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25678v1 公告类型：新 摘要：人工智能（AI）日益融入科学工作，但研究人员可能在不同研究任务中对其使用的评价并不一致。本研究考察了来自STEM以及医学和健康科学领域的国际自选样本中3785名博士生对AI的任务特定态度，这些博士生参与了《自然》2025年研究生调查。我们分析了受访者对使用AI撰写研究文章、收集和分析数据、设计实验、追踪科学文献以及总结文献的舒适度。潜在类别分析识别出四种不同的态度概况。主导概况反映了“分工”模式，其中AI在文献相关任务中被广泛接受，但在与智力贡献密切相关的活动（如写作、数据分析和实验设计）中遭到抵制。“现状”概况在所有任务中普遍感到不适，“全能”概况则与之相反。
tldr: 本研究通过分析3785名博士生的态度，发现AI在科学工作中的接受度因任务而异，主流观点支持将AI用于文献相关任务，但抵制其在写作、数据分析和实验设计等核心智力活动中的应用。
en_tdlr: This study, based on 3,785 PhD researchers, reveals that AI acceptance in scientific work varies by task, with a dominant preference for AI in literature-related tasks but resistance to its use in core intellectual activities like writing, data analysis, and experimental design.
